questions.question: Which protocol is primarily used for sending email between mail servers?
questions.explanation: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is the standard push protocol used for sending and relaying emails between mail servers.

questions.question: Which protocol is primarily used by an email client to retrieve emails from a mail server?
questions.explanation: Post Office Protocol version 3 (POP3) is designed for email clients to download and retrieve messages from a mail server.

questions.question: What is the default port number for SMTP?
questions.explanation: Standard unencrypted SMTP server-to-server relay communication uses well-known TCP port 25.

questions.question: What is the default port number for POP3?
questions.explanation: The standard port for unencrypted POP3 mail retrieval service is TCP port 110.

questions.question: Which protocol is primarily used to transfer web pages between a web browser and a web server?
questions.explanation: Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is the foundational protocol used for transmitting web documents and resources across the World Wide Web.

questions.question: What is the default port number of HTTP?
questions.explanation: Standard unencrypted HTTP web traffic listens on well-known TCP port 80.

questions.question: What is the default port number of HTTPS?
questions.explanation: Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS) operates over TLS/SSL on standard TCP port 443.

questions.question: HTTPS is essentially HTTP combined with:
questions.explanation: HTTPS consists of standard HTTP communication layered over an encrypted Transport Layer Security (TLS) or Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) tunnel.

questions.question: Which protocol provides encryption and authentication for HTTPS?
questions.explanation: Transport Layer Security (TLS) provides end-to-end data encryption, server authentication, and message integrity for HTTPS.

questions.question: Which is the modern successor to SSL for securing network communication?
questions.explanation: TLS (Transport Layer Security) was developed as the modern, more secure cryptographic successor to deprecated SSL protocols.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most secure modern protocol version among these?
questions.explanation: TLS 1.3 is the latest, most secure cryptographic standard, featuring improved handshake efficiency and removing obsolete, vulnerable cipher suites.

questions.question: Which technology is responsible for protecting HTTP traffic against eavesdropping and tampering in HTTPS?
questions.explanation: TLS provides cryptographic privacy and integrity protection, preventing unauthorized interception, eavesdropping, and tampering.

questions.question: Which SMTP port is commonly used for message submission with encryption such as STARTTLS?
questions.explanation: Port 587 is the standard submission port defined in RFC 6409 for mail clients to submit messages to an outgoing SMTP server using STARTTLS.

questions.question: Which port is traditionally associated with SMTP over implicit TLS (SMTPS)?
questions.explanation: Port 465 was originally assigned and is widely utilized for secure email submission using implicit TLS (SMTPS).

questions.question: Which port is used by POP3 over implicit TLS?
questions.explanation: POP3S (POP3 over SSL/TLS) connects securely to mail servers over dedicated TCP port 995.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is normally used to request a resource from a web server?
questions.explanation: The HTTP GET method is designed to retrieve data or resources specified by a given URI from a web server.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code indicates that a requested resource was successfully retrieved?
questions.explanation: HTTP status code 200 OK indicates that the client's request succeeded and the requested payload is delivered.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code indicates that the requested resource was not found?
questions.explanation: HTTP status code 404 Not Found signals that the server cannot locate the requested URI resource.

questions.question: Which statement about POP3 is correct?
options: It is primarily used to send outgoing email
It is primarily used to retrieve email from a mail server
It is used to resolve domain names
It is used to transfer web pages
questions.explanation: POP3 is an incoming mail protocol designed for client endpoints to retrieve and download emails from a remote mailbox server.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes TLS?
options: TLS is an email retrieval protocol
TLS provides security services such as encryption, authentication, and integrity
TLS assigns IP addresses to hosts
TLS translates domain names into IP addresses
questions.explanation: Transport Layer Security (TLS) operates above the transport layer to provide confidentiality (encryption), authentication, and message integrity.

questions.question: Which protocol is primarily used for monitoring and managing network devices?
questions.explanation: Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is widely used by network administrators to monitor, configure, and collect statistics from network hardware.

questions.question: Which port is commonly used by SNMP for receiving queries from a management system?
questions.explanation: SNMP agents listen on UDP port 161 for requests (Get, Set, GetNext) sent from the Network Management Station (NMS).

questions.question: Which port is commonly used by SNMP for sending traps to a management system?
questions.explanation: SNMP traps (unsolicited notifications generated by agents to alert managers of asynchronous events) are received on UDP port 162.

questions.question: Which SNMP component stores managed device information in a structured database?
questions.explanation: Management Information Base (MIB) is a hierarchically structured database describing managed device objects and parameters referenced via OIDs.

questions.question: Which protocol is a link-state interior gateway protocol (IGP)?
questions.explanation: Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) is the primary open-standard link-state interior gateway protocol used within an Autonomous System.

questions.question: What algorithm is primarily used by OSPF to calculate the shortest path?
questions.explanation: OSPF constructs a complete network topology map and executes Dijkstra's Shortest Path First (SPF) algorithm to calculate loop-free shortest paths.

questions.question: Which metric does OSPF primarily use to select the best path?
questions.explanation: OSPF uses 'Cost' as its metric, which is inversely proportional to link bandwidth (Cost = Reference Bandwidth / Interface Bandwidth).

questions.question: Which OSPF packet type is used to discover and maintain neighbor relationships?
questions.explanation: OSPF Hello packets are periodically multicast between adjacent routers to discover neighbors, establish adjacencies, and monitor link availability.

questions.question: Which protocol uses hop count as its primary routing metric?
questions.explanation: Routing Information Protocol (RIP) uses simple hop count (number of intermediate routers) as its sole metric for selecting paths.

questions.question: What is the maximum hop count supported by RIP before a route is considered unreachable?
questions.explanation: In RIP, a hop count of 15 is the maximum valid metric; a hop count of 16 represents infinity (an unreachable route).

questions.question: Which routing protocol is classified as a distance-vector protocol?
questions.explanation: RIP is a classic distance-vector routing protocol that uses the Bellman-Ford algorithm to share routing tables with immediate neighbors.

questions.question: Which version of RIP supports classless routing and VLSM?
questions.explanation: RIPv2 introduced support for subnet masks in routing updates, enabling Variable Length Subnet Masking (VLSM) and classless routing (CIDR).

questions.question: Which protocol is commonly described as an advanced distance-vector or hybrid routing protocol?
questions.explanation: Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) combines distance-vector ease of configuration with link-state rapid convergence, making it an advanced distance-vector protocol.

questions.question: Which algorithm is associated with EIGRP for calculating loop-free routes?
questions.explanation: EIGRP uses the Diffusing Update Algorithm (DUAL) to guarantee loop-free operation and provide fast convergence using feasible successors.

questions.question: Which of the following is a metric component used by EIGRP?
questions.explanation: EIGRP's composite metric formula primarily uses minimum bandwidth and cumulative delay by default (along with optional reliability, load, and MTU).

questions.question: Which routing protocol is primarily used for routing between autonomous systems?
questions.explanation: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) is the standardized Exterior Gateway Protocol (EGP) that connects different Autonomous Systems across the Internet.

questions.question: Which transport-layer protocol does BGP use?
questions.explanation: BGP establishes reliable peer-to-peer peering sessions over Transmission Control Protocol (TCP).

questions.question: What is the well-known TCP port number used by BGP?
questions.explanation: BGP peers exchange routing updates over well-known TCP destination port 179.

questions.question: Which BGP attribute is used to influence the preferred outbound path within an autonomous system?
questions.explanation: The Local Preference (LOCAL_PREF) attribute is propagated throughout an AS to instruct internal routers on which exit path to prefer for outbound traffic.

questions.question: Which protocol is primarily responsible for reporting errors and providing diagnostic information at the IP layer?
questions.explanation: Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) operates alongside IP to convey error reports, control messages, and diagnostic feedback.

questions.question: Which ICMP message is commonly used by the ping utility?
questions.explanation: Ping sends ICMP Echo Request messages (Type 8) to test reachability, expecting ICMP Echo Reply messages (Type 0) in return.

questions.question: Which ICMP message is commonly associated with the traceroute function in IPv4?
questions.explanation: Traceroute sends packets with incrementing TTL values; intermediate routers decrement TTL to 0, discard the packet, and return an ICMP Time Exceeded message.

questions.question: Which protocol resolves an IPv4 address to a MAC address on a local network?
questions.explanation: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) translates a known Layer 3 IPv4 address into the corresponding Layer 2 physical MAC address on a broadcast domain.

questions.question: ARP operates primarily between which OSI layers?
questions.explanation: ARP bridges Layer 3 (Network layer IP addressing) with Layer 2 (Data Link layer physical addressing).

questions.question: What type of Ethernet destination address is normally used in an ARP Request?
questions.explanation: ARP Requests are transmitted to the Ethernet broadcast address (FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF) so that all hosts on the local network receive and process the inquiry.

questions.question: Which ARP message contains the MAC address corresponding to the requested IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: The target machine responds to an ARP Request with a unicast ARP Reply containing its hardware MAC address.

questions.question: A router has two possible OSPF routes to the same destination with different costs. Which route will normally be preferred?
questions.explanation: OSPF always prefers the route with the lowest cumulative metric (Cost), selecting the shortest and most bandwidth-efficient path.

questions.question: A RIP router receives a route with a metric of 16. What does this indicate?
questions.explanation: In RIP, metric 16 represents infinity, indicating that the target network has failed or is unreachable.

questions.question: If an IPv4 host knows the destination IP address but does not know its MAC address on the local network, which protocol will it use?
questions.explanation: The host broadcasts an Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) query on the local subnet to discover the MAC address associated with the known destination IP.

questions.question: Which combination is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) establishes peering sessions over TCP port 179. (OSPF uses Cost, RIP uses Bellman-Ford/Hop Count, and SNMP uses UDP 161).
